newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 sees unemployment as Europe's biggest problem.
newsitem.headline: G10 sees unemployment as Europe's biggest problem.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said structural unemployment remained the main problem of continental European economies.
Tietmeyer told reporters that structural rigidities in European labour markets were the cause of jobless problems and added that monetary policy had done all it could to help job creation.
"On the one hand there is continued macroeconomic growth and this will continue according to expectations, but the problem is structural problems responsible for unemployment," Tietmeyer said.
"This is the main problem in continental Europe," he said after chairing a monthly meeting of the Group of 10 central bank governors at the Bank for International Settlements.
Tietmeyer said the central bank governors hoped that the expected continued growth of European economies would begin creating new jobs.
He said some labour market reforms were already under way and needed to be continued in order to boost job creation.
"It is not monetary policy that will solve these structural problems," he told reporters.
"Monetary policy has to stay on the line where it is now," Tietmeyer added.
Asked which structural barriers to job creation he was referring to, Tietmeyer said, "structural rigidities in the labour markets, as I have said many times".
"Also for some areas (there are) too high labour costs," he said without elaborating.

Tietmeyer said the G10 governors saw signs of some increase in real investment in Europe but these investments tended to be in boosting productivity in existing sectors rather than in creating new business sectors.
"This is making sectors more competitive but at the cost sometimes of (creating) new employment," he said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
